newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BHP Port Headland iron project ready mid-98.
newsitem.headline: BHP Port Headland iron project ready mid-98.

text.p: A Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) project at Australia's Port Headland with a two million tonne-per-annum capacity of hot briquetted iron (HBI) will be on stream by mid-1998, an official said on Tuesday. "We expect the first shipments by mid-1998," said Tom Albracht, the firm's market development manager for HBI.
He was addressing the Third Annual Asian Steel Summit being held in Hong Kong.
"The project is now at the halfway mark, with completion in just over 12 months," he said.

HBI production would allow BHP to participate more fully in the Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) market, Albracht said. EAF steel production technology, cheaper than traditional blast furnace methods, was expected to grow to 44 percent of total steel production by the year 2010, up from 32 percent in 1995, BHP estimated.
Using HBI lowers residual material and allows the production of better steels with EAF technology.
But if all HBI manufacturing projects were completed, a possible oversupply could develop by the year 2000, Albracht said.

"A price eroding oversupply is possible in 2005 if only a portion of the other announced projects are developed," he told the industry gathering. Ninety percent of demand for HBI would largely be focused in North America and in East Asia, Albracht projected.

The expected merchant capacity, if projects under construction and likely projects materialised, would jump to 16 million tonnes by the year 2000, compared to the current 3.5 million tonnes per year, he said. -- Mishi Saran (852) 2843 6358
